interpretation: Absolute total CPU saved per tick is nearly equal (OA/PG 1.0013); system CPU saved per tick is 5.55% lower on OA and voluntary switches saved per tick 3.22% lower. This is consistent with a roughly fixed per-tick coordination component, not an exact constant or causal identification. OA baseline user CPU per tick is 3.13 times PG; this larger residual/useful-work proxy explains much of the smaller percentage gain descriptively.

The system CPU/context-switch reductions support reduced scheduling/wakeup overhead as a plausible mechanism, but process counters cannot assign it to futexes or individual callbacks. Telemetry is Off; no direct wake/job counts were recorded.
PG128-square/8 AI versus OA256-square/11 AI differ in trajectory, team counts, callback families, data sizes and game lengths; map size is not an isolated intervention.
Whole-process wait4 CPU includes startup/load/shutdown; inner wall is separately measured. Saved user CPU can include scheduling/coordination work and is not a pure useful-work measure.
After the campaign, residual callback/user CPU and wake frequency could be profiled under representative states; no profiler or workload was launched for this audit.
Endpoint/tick/winner matching complements prior latest per-tick qualification; ordinary timing receipts are not new per-tick checksum proof.

Two timing repeats of fixed workload establish no population confidence interval.

immediate-run-followup/design-proof.json.conclusion: runDone is redundant for parallel immediate run barrier under existing one-owner run/lifecycle contract. inFlight alone suffices AFTER owner invoke exhausted next. This is a smaller source design, not a measured win.

source_refs.public_run: 1420; no tryRun API in this header

proof: next fetch_add is a single monotonically ordered claim stream for this generation. Owner invoke returns only after obtaining index>=count, so every valid index has already been claimed. Owner callback exceptions are caught and loop continues.

Owner callbacks have returned when owner invoke returns. Any other valid claimed callback belongs to worker which incremented inFlight under mutex before unlocking/invoke; worker decrements only after invoke and Trace epilogue return.

Owner locks same mutex after own invoke and waits inFlight==0. This covers all remaining worker callbacks and their results/errors; mutex unlock/relock publishes their ordinary writes to owner. No extra per-job done atomic needed.

Late worker may observe generation after owner cleared job, but its next claim is already exhausted, so empty function is never invoked. Worker registers before reading count/next under existing publication protocol.

If next run begins, publication waits inFlight0 under global and writes count/function/next/generation while holding global. A registering worker either holds old registration that blocks rewrite or sees new generation/data after rewrite; no concurrent count/function mutation during invoke.

Optional presentation/maintenance may delay a worker reaching generation but cannot leave unclaimed required indices after owner claim exhaustion. Worker outside invoke is not needed to establish completed barrier.
Nested run executes inline through active branch and never replaces outer generation. n0/n1/no-worker paths independent. Errors remain serialized under mutex then rethrown only after barrier.

runDone trace snapshot guard adds no needed protection when traceRunActive covers active owner generation; lifecycle/reset ownership assumptions unchanged. Public API not arbitrary concurrent run/configure safe.

CallbackEnd/Complete/workerMetrics lock becomes Trace-only; exception lock retained all modes. Waits-mode executed accounting unchanged.
After owner invoke, incomplete=inFlight!=0 and wait predicate inFlight==0. Worker registration/decrement and final notify unchanged.
Keep all count/next/generation publication and worker lifetime synchronization exactly.
tests_before_experiment: Back-to-back many generations with tiny batches, owner wins all claims and late worker enters zero-job invoke.

Nested immediate run, worker/owner throws, repeated run after error, telemetry Off/Waits/Trace snapshot/reset contracts.
Run while presentation/graphics/maintenance active and lifecycle drain; same existing single-owner constraints.
Final source assembly/source inspection confirms Off successful callbacks have no shared mutex; no timing claim until native residual cost and separate matched micro justify.
